strengths: Novel conceptual framework: Treating distribution parameters as actions elegantly redefines the agent-environment boundary and provides a principled unified approach to discrete, continuous, and mixed action spaces

Rigorous theoretical contributions: Theorem 4.2 establishes the policy gradient theorem for DPPG; Propositions 4.4-4.5 prove variance reduction over LR and RP estimators; convergence analysis (Theorem A.7) properly extends DPG guarantees to the parameter-space MDP

Principled handling of bias-variance tradeoff: Paper acknowledges that lower variance can increase bias due to critic complexity and proposes ICL as a targeted solution, demonstrating sophisticated understanding

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 20 environments with proper statistical reporting (95% bootstrapped CIs), multiple baselines, ablation studies, and insightful bandit experiments visualizing critic learning dynamics
Practical unification: Demonstrates the same algorithm works across diverse action types without sensitive hyperparameter tuning, which is conceptually appealing for practitioners
weaknesses: Modest and inconsistent empirical improvements: Performance gains over TD3 are often marginal; on discrete actions (Figure 5), confidence intervals substantially overlap between DPAC and AC-ST, with AC-ST outperforming DPAC on several tasks, contradicting theoretical advantages

Interpolated Critic Learning lacks principled justification: Linear interpolation choice (Eq. 13) appears ad-hoc with no justification versus alternatives; motivation via toy bandit problems doesn't validate effectiveness in deep RL; no sensitivity analysis on interpolation weight or ablations on critic architecture

Uncharacterized increase in critic complexity: Paper acknowledges that parameter-space input makes critic learning harder but provides no systematic analysis of this bias-variance tradeoff; for high-cardinality discrete actions, parameter vectors become high-dimensional with unclear consequences

Discrete action results contradict central claims: Despite claiming to provide 'first unbiased RP-style estimator with low variance in discrete setting,' Figure 5 shows statistically indistinguishable or worse performance compared to AC-ST, raising fundamental questions about theory-practice gap

Limited evaluation scope: Experiments restricted to locomotion/control (MuJoCo/DMC); missing evaluation on high-dimensional discrete spaces where advantages should manifest most clearly; no mixed action space experiments; missing comparisons to other unified frameworks

Theory-practice gap: Convergence theorem assumes on-policy linear function approximation while DPAC is evaluated off-policy with deep networks; variance reduction proofs assume perfect critic, which never occurs in practice, weakening practical applicability of theoretical results

Hyperparameter inconsistencies undermine claims: DPAC uses learnable σ ∈ [0.05, 0.2] while TD3 uses fixed σ=0.1; claimed 'without hyperparameter tuning' conflicts with this additional tuning that favors DPAC

Parameter-space MDP transformation properties unexplored: Equations 8-9 create fundamentally different MDP structure; potential consequences for optimization landscape, exploration difficulty, and conditioning not discussed or analyzed

strengths: Novel distribution-as-actions framework providing conceptual unification of diverse action spaces with elegant reformulation of agent-environment boundary
Strong theoretical analysis with rigorous proofs of lower variance for DA-PG vs. LR and RP estimators (Propositions 4.4-4.5) and convergence guarantees (Theorem C.7)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation spanning continuous (MuJoCo/DMC), discrete (Gym/MinAtar), high-dimensional discrete, and hybrid (PAMDP) control with rigorous statistical analysis (10 seeds, bootstrap CIs, paired t-tests)
Interpolated Critic Learning (ICL) is well-motivated with clear empirical benefits demonstrated through bandit visualization and consistent improvements (Figure 7, Table 1 with p<0.01)
Excellent reproducibility: extensive appendices with complete hyperparameters, implementation details, promised code release
Proper generalization showing DPG as special case (Proposition 4.3) and extending DPG convergence theory to DA-PG
weaknesses: Concurrent work by Todorov (2025b) on D-MDP formulation simultaneously develops similar core conceptual contribution, diminishing novelty claims at a top-tier venue

ICL is biased (acknowledged by authors) yet lacks principled justification: arbitrary design choices (why linear interpolation? why uniform ω?), no convergence theory for algorithms with ICL, and principled importance weighting deferred to future work despite being central

Empirical improvements are marginal and inconsistent: continuous control shows minimal gains over TD3/RP-AC often within error bars (Figure 3), discrete control comparable to DQN/EAC (Figure 5 cols 1-2), clear advantage only in narrow high-dimensional discrete setting

Bias-variance tradeoff unresolved: while DA-PG has theoretically lower per-state variance, critic learning in high-dimensional parameter space creates higher bias. No quantification of when variance reduction outweighs increased bias. Figure 9 shows DA-AC w/o ICL performs catastrophically, suggesting substantial bias problems

Unclear practical advantages: practitioners have little guidance on when to adopt DA-AC. For continuous control, TD3/SAC already work excellently; for discrete control, DQN/EPG dominate; for hybrid, PATD3 competitive. No compelling use case established
Limited ablations: DA-AC vs w/o-ICL conflates DA-PG and ICL effects; no systematic exploration of interpolation strategy alternatives; sensitivity to ω ∈ [0,1] not studied
Convergence analysis (Theorem C.7) relies on unrealistic linear function approximation assumption; gaps in theory for practical deep RL algorithms with ICL

Comprehensive and rigorous experimental evaluation across 40+ environments spanning continuous (MuJoCo, DMC), discrete (Gym, MinAtar), high-dimensional discrete, and hybrid (PAMDP) control settings with proper statistical reporting
